newsitem.title: USA: Baseball's Schott sells dealership, report says.
newsitem.headline: Baseball's Schott sells dealership, report says.

text.p: Under pressure from General Motors Corp, Cincinnati Reds owner Marge Schott has completed the sale of her Chevrolet-Geo dealership for undisclosed terms, the Cincinnati Enquirer newspaper reported Thursday.

GM, in a complaint filed in December with Ohio's dealer licensing board, alleged Schott falsified 1995 records on 57 auto sales to meet sales quotas. Using employees' and friends' names as fictional buyers, she then hid cars involved in the bogus sales on her estate, GM said.
GM sought to terminate her as a Chevy dealer but later said it would permit the sale if it approves the terms. A GM spokesman could not immediately be reached.
Baseball's National League has said it also will look into the matter. Schott allegedly used the names of several Reds employees, without their knowledge, as fictitious buyers, the paper has said.

Schott remains suspended by the National League through 1998 from Reds daily operations for comments she has made in interviews about Adolf Hitler, African-Americans, working women and Jews. She had also been suspended in 1993.

Ronald Joseph, chief executive officer of the Joseph Group which bought the dealership, told the paper Schott would be a consultant to the new owners. The dealership, in suburban Montgomery, will be called Montgomery Chevrolet.
GM has said Schott may retain another dealership, Schott Buick, in suburban Norwood, which was not involved in the current controversy.
